rv.q: Sameena Hussain has delivered such a big-hearted show that goes out of its way to engage its audience.
Planet Omar is an exercise in anti-othering.

If the slightly underpowered scenes don’t amount to a great adventure, it still culminates charmingly in an act of grown-up heroism in which two enemies set their differences aside and begin an unlikely friendship – a lesson for the young and old.
Sadly, this production delivers very little of any of them.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this adaptation of Zanib Mian's popular books, with most finding charm in its representation but one dismissing it as dramatically flat and unimaginative, relying on stereotypes over genuine theatricality.
